bib.title: GUI-R1 : A Generalist R1-Style Vision-Language Action Model For GUI Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: GUI-R1: A Generalist R1-Style Vision-Language Action Model For GUI Agents. Run Luo, Lu Wang, Wanwei He, Longze Chen, Jiaming Li, Min Yang, Xiaobo Xia (SIAT-CAS, UCAS, NUS). Preprint, arXiv:2504.10458v4 [cs.CV], 1 Oct 2025, marked "Technical report". No peer-reviewed venue is stated.

COVERAGE: 40,740 of 40,740 chars read, which is the whole extraction. The extraction did not report page boundaries, so I cite printed page numbers (pp. 1-9, then references from p. 10). Pages 1-9 hold the body, tables and ablations. References were read through [29] and the extraction ends mid-reference, so the last few are truncated. There is no appendix with results. Figures 1, 3, 4 and 5 came through as axis labels only, so no values can be read from them.

CLAIMS
1. GUI-R1 is the first rule-based RFT (GRPO) framework aimed at high-level GUI action prediction. It uses one unified action space across Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and Web.
   - number: none
   - setup: base model Qwen2.5-VL 3B and 7B, trained on GUI-R1-3K.
   - quote: "we propose GUI-R1, the first reinforcement learning framework designed to enhance the GUI capabilities of LVLMs in high-level real-world task scenarios, through unified action space rule modeling"
   - where: p.1 abstract

2. The headline data-efficiency claim is that 3K RL examples beat OS-Atlas, which was SFT'd on millions of examples. The paper is inconsistent on the ratio.
   - number: 0.02% (3K vs 13M) in the abstract and intro; 0.2% (3K vs 14M) in Sec 4.2; ~14M collected in Sec 3.3. Treat the ratio as unreliable; 3K vs roughly 13-14M is the safe form.
   - setup: eight benchmarks; zero-shot with a unified prompt across all compared methods.
   - quote: "GUI-R1 achieves superior performance using only 0.02% of the data (3K vs. 13M) compared to previous state-of-the-art methods like OS-Atlas across eight benchmarks spanning three different platforms (mobile, desktop, and web)". Sec 4.2 says: "using only 0.2% of the data (3K vs. 14M)".
   - where: p.1 abstract; p.6

3. At 3B, RFT beats SFT on the same 3K data for grounding (SFT'd on the identical GUI-R1-3K, marked *).
   - number: ScreenSpot 80.08 vs 63.55; ScreenSpot-Pro 25.23 vs 13.80; +26.3% and +82.8% relative.
   - setup: Qwen2.5-VL-3B; the SFT baseline is trained for one epoch on GUI-R1-3K.
   - quote: "at the 3B scale, GUI-R1 achieves substantial gains over SFT models on ScreenSpot (80.08 vs. 63.55) and ScreenSpot-Pro (25.23 vs. 13.80), representing improvements of 26.3% and 82.8%, respectively."
   - where: p.6
   - Caveat: the 63.55 and 80.08 averages are not in Table 1, which lists only per-column values. I could not check them.

4. On low-level tasks, GUI-R1 beats the base model and SFT'd variants at 3B. The 7B gain is small.
   - number: 3B overall 80.88 vs base 55.65. 7B overall 83.30 vs base 79.05, 7B-SFT 80.09, OS-Atlas-7B 70.07, UI-R1-3B 70.85, GPT-4o 54.46.
   - setup: Table 2, four benchmarks (GUI-Act-Web, OmniAct-Web, OmniAct-Desktop, AndroidControl-Low), Type/GR/SR averaged.
   - quote: "with the average success rate increasing from 55.65 to 80.88 at the 3B scale." Also "our model achieves a 10-point improvement at the 3B scale" over UI-R1.
   - where: p.6-7, Table 2

5. On high-level tasks, GUI-R1 is state of the art among the compared models. The 3B gain over UI-R1 is modest; the 7B model improves over its base mainly on grounding (GR) and Type.
   - number: Table 3 overall: GUI-R1-3B 49.75, GUI-R1-7B 56.13, UI-R1-3B 46.35, Qwen2.5-VL-7B base 50.53, 7B-SFT 50.97, OS-Atlas-7B 44.88, GPT-4o 28.69. Text: +21.06 absolute over GPT-4o at 3B; average +3.4 over UI-R1 at 3B; "27.2% lead" in SR on GUI-Odyssey.
   - setup: AndroidControl-High and GUI-Odyssey (cross-app, 203 apps).
   - quote: "compared to the closed-source model GPT-4o, our 3B-scale method achieves an absolute improvement of 21.06". Also "our model achieves an average improvement of 3.4 points at the 3B scale, with a particularly notable 27.2% lead in the step success rate on GUI-Odyssey."
   - where: p.7-8, Table 3
   - Caveat: GUI-R1-3B's GUI-Odyssey SR is 41.33 against UI-R1-3B's 32.49 in Table 3. GUI-R1-7B is only +5.6 overall over the untrained 7B base.

6. Grounding at 7B (Table 1, ScreenSpot-Pro columns): GUI-R1-7B beats OS-Atlas-7B on most ScreenSpot-Pro categories.
   - number: Dev text 49.4 vs 33.1; Scientific text 55.6 vs 37.5; Office text 58.7 vs 33.9; OS text 42.1 vs 27.1. On ScreenSpot Desktop icon, 73.6 vs 62.8. On ScreenSpot Web text, 91.3 vs 90.8.
   - quote: "GUI-R1-7B 49.4 4.8 38.9 8.4 23.9 6.3 55.6 11.8 58.7 26.4 42.1 16.9 91.3 75.7 91.8 73.6"
   - where: p.7, Table 1
   - Caveat: GUI-R1-7B does not win every column. In CAD text, OS-Atlas-7B scores 12.2 against GUI-R1-7B's 23.9, so GUI-R1 is ahead there. GUI-R1-3B scores 26.4 in CAD text. OS-Atlas-7B beats GUI-R1-7B on Web icon 74.2 vs 75.7? That is GUI-R1 ahead, so none are clear losses in this row; the bolding in the extraction is garbled, so check the original table.

7. Data filtering with Qwen2.5-VL-7B produced GUI-R1-3K.
   - number: ~14M collected (about 30K of it high-level, from OS-Atlas); 140K low-level and 1.5K high-level after filtering; 1.5K low-level sampled; 3K total.
   - setup: 10 rollouts per example from Qwen2.5-VL-7B, dropping examples with estimated accuracy 0 or 1.
   - quote: "We remove the problems with an estimated accuracy of 0 or 1 to ensure a stable training process, resulting in 140K low-level data and 1.5K high-level data."
   - where: p.5
   - Sources: FineWeb, UIBert, AMEX, RICOSCA, SeeClick and OS-Atlas pretraining data.

8. Ablation on data quality and resolution: filtered data converges faster and to a higher ceiling, and doubling the image resolution helps further.
   - number: resolution 1,048,576 to 2,097,152 pixels. The reward curves are only in Figure 4, with no numeric values.
   - setup: three conditions, high-quality/high-res, high-quality/low-res, low-quality/low-res; training reward vs steps.
   - quote: "we increase the image resolution to twice its original size (from 1,048,576 pixels to 2,097,152 pixels)"
   - where: p.8, Fig 4

9. Ablation on reward coefficients (Table 4): a smaller format weight and larger accuracy weight performs best.
   - number: alpha=0.2, beta=0.8 gives overall 49.75; 0.5/0.5 gives 47.72; 0.8/0.2 gives 46.48.
   - setup: GUI-R1-3B on AndroidControl-High and GUI-Odyssey.
   - quote: "0.2 0.8 58.04 56.24 46.55 54.84 41.52 41.33 49.75 / 0.5 0.5 ... 47.72 / 0.8 0.2 ... 46.48"
   - where: p.9, Table 4
   - Caveat: the 0.8/0.2 row has the same per-column values as UI-R1-3B in Table 3 (overall 46.35 there, 46.48 here). Suspicious duplication.
   - Caveat: there is NO ablation that removes individual reward terms (R_act, R_point, R_text). Only the format vs accuracy weights were varied.

10. Reward design is fully rule-based and verifiable.
    - number: R_o = alpha*R_f + beta*R_acc, with R_acc = R_act + R_point + R_text. R_act is exact match. R_point is 1 if the click is inside the ground-truth bbox. R_text is 1 if semantic F1 > 0.5.
    - setup: GRPO advantage is the group-normalized reward, with a KL constraint.
    - quote: "Rtext = 1 if F1(otext, gttext) > 0.5, 0 otherwise." and "Ro = αRf + βRacc"
    - where: p.4

11. Training dynamics: format reward converges early. Accuracy reward drives the later learning signal. Response length first falls, then rises. No "aha moment".
    - number: none
    - quote: "the mean response length first decreases and then gradually increases, but the “aha moment” does not occur."
    - where: p.9, Fig 5

12. Training setup.
    - number: SFT one epoch (LLaMA Factory); RFT nine epochs (EasyR1); 8×A100-80G.
    - quote: "employ the LLaMA Factory [25] framework for one epoch of training to avoid overfitting. For RFT, we use the EasyR1 [26] framework for training over nine epochs."
    - where: p.6

LIMITS
- The authors speculate that the lack of an "aha moment" is due to single-image, non-interactive training. They say multi-image tasks in interactive environments could be future work. Future work also covers multi-agent collaboration and error correction.
- All evaluation is offline, step-wise, on static benchmarks. There is no live-environment success rate such as OSWorld or AndroidWorld.
- No UI-TARS numbers are reported. UI-TARS is only cited as related work. The comparisons are OS-Atlas, UI-R1, SeeClick, UGround, CogAgent, ShowUI, Aria-GUI, Claude, GPT-4o and the SFT baselines.
- The SFT baseline is one epoch on only 3K examples. It is a same-data comparison, not a tuned SFT recipe, and it does not show that SFT on large data would lose.
- The training data is drawn from the same families as the test benchmarks (OS-Atlas, AMEX and others), so out-of-distribution generalization is claimed but not isolated.
- The 7B gains over the untrained Qwen2.5-VL-7B base are small on several metrics. Base 7B GR on AndroidControl-Low is 87.08, higher than GUI-R1-7B's 84.02.
- Internal inconsistencies: 0.02% vs 0.2% and 13M vs 14M; the Table 4 vs Table 3 duplicate row; and the text says "GUI-Act-Web [29]" where the citation is [30].
- The paper concedes SFT's weakness only as a claim ("small-scale SFT data even leads to performance degradation on some metrics such as GR on AndroidControl-Low").

BUILDS ON
- DeepSeek-R1 and GRPO (Guo et al. 2025; DeepSeekMath, Shao et al. 2024), for the RFT paradigm.
- UI-R1 (Lu et al. 2025), concurrent RFT on low-level grounding.
- OS-Atlas (Wu et al. 2024), SeeClick (Cheng et al. 2024), UGround (Gou et al. 2024) and UI-TARS (Qin et al. 2025).
- Visual-RFT, Vision-R1, R1-V, VLM-R1 and MM-Eureka for vision RL rewards.
- Qwen2.5-VL (Bai et al. 2025), EasyR1 (Zheng et al. 2025) and LLaMA Factory (Zheng et al. 2024).
- Benchmarks: AndroidControl (Li et al. 2024), GUI-Odyssey (Lu et al. 2024), ScreenSpot, ScreenSpot-Pro, GUI-Act-Web, OmniAct.

CODE: no code in the paper. Repository: https://github.com/ritzz-ai/GUI-R1.git (p.1). Output format and action enum, verbatim from the prompt on p.4:
`<think>...</think> <answer>[‘action’: enum[complete,close/delete,press home,click,press back,type,select,scroll,enter], ‘point’: [x, y], ‘input text’: ‘no input text [default]’]</answer>`

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): radar charts of GUI-R1 vs Qwen2.5-VL base, SFT and UI-R1 across the eight benchmarks, in three panels (grounding, low-level, high-level). It gives a quick visual of the gap, but the values are not recoverable from text.
- Fig 2 (p.3): framework overview. The policy produces think/answer outputs, the three rule rewards (text, point, action) are computed, and policy-gradient updates are made with a reference model. This is the clearest summary of the method.
- Fig 3 (p.5): GUI-R1-3K image-category and action-type distribution and difficulty.
- Fig 4 (p.8): reward vs training steps for data quality and resolution.
- Fig 5 (p.9): format reward, accuracy reward, PG loss and response length over about 90 steps.

PROBLEMS
- The figure and table text is partly garbled. Bolding is lost, and some cells run together, such as "33.84.8".
- No embedded instructions were found in the PDF.
- The 63.55 and 80.08 SFT and RFT averages could not be verified from the tables.
- The reference list is truncated in the extraction after [29].
